sentences.text: Briefly stated, the facts of the case are that the complainant lodged a written Report (Exhibit- P/8) dated 02.07.1987 in Police Station, Arnod, Pratapgarh alleging inter alia that his daughter, the prosecutrix, had left for her in-laws' place in village Bhadwas Kala about 4 months ago and went missing.

He further alleged that pursuant to efforts made at their end, they found the prosecutrix to be living in Dhakarkhedi, District Bhilawara with one Bheria Meena, to whom she was sold under the customary practice of 'Nata Pratha' by Bumba Pathan, Baras Khan, Jagdish,
Sohan Lal, Cheeman Lala Balai and the wives of Ambalala and Jagdish.
3. The Police filed a charge-sheet against all the accused persons for the offences under Sections 366/120B, 376, 344/120B of the Indian Penal Code (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC').

The competent court after committing the case, sent it to the trial court, which framed charges qua appellant No.1, under Sections 366/120B,
376/109-344/120B of the IPC, while charges under Section 366/120B, 376-344/120B of the IPC were framed against other appellants namely, Gautam, Jagdish @ Jagla and Gopal @Jabba.
(Uploaded on 06/10/2025 at 05:21:15 PM) (3 of 8)

4. The prosecution produced PW-1 - Dr. K.L. Porwal; PW-2 - Babulal; PW-3 - Kalu; PW-4 - Nanuram; PW-5 - Gopi; PW-6 - Bhola; PW-7 - Chhogalal; PW-8 - Mohan; PW-9 - Omprakash;
PW-10 - Mst. K; PW-11 - Rajesh Kumar; PW-12 - Narendra Kumar; PW-13 - Vakhthram; PW-14 - Tej Singh; PW-15 - Bamba @ Alimkhan; PW-16 - Nanda; PW-17 - Laldas; PW-18 - Thavarchand Damor - the then Dy. Superintendent of Police, Pratapgarh - Investigating Officer in the witness box, whose statements were recorded.
The prosecution also exhibited certain documents (Exhibit P/1 to P/9) in order to prove the charges framed against the accused-appellant persons.
5. The accused persons did not produce any evidence in their defence.
However, their statements under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were recorded, wherein they stated that they had been falsely implicated because of animosity.

6. The trial court after appreciating the evidence on record had acquitted the appellant no.1 - Kesu Ram for the offence under Section 376 of the IPC and other appellants-accused persons for the offence under Sections 344/120B of the IPC.

However, the appellant no.1 - Kesu Ram was convicted for the offence under Section 366/120B of the IPC while other appellants namely, Jagdish @ Jagla @ Jagannath, Gopal @Jabba and Gautam were convicted for the offence under Section 376 of the Kesha Ram vs State Of Rajasthan on 3 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91673029/

sentences.text: 7. Mr Praveen Vyas, learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the trial court has not scrutinized the prosecution evidence in light of the fact that the written report dated 02.07.1987 (Exhibit- P/8) based on which the FIR was registered on 04.07.1987 does not contain the allegation of rape being (Uploaded on 06/10/2025 at 05:21:15 PM) (4 of 8) [CRLA-207/1996] committed by the accused-appellants.
Furthermore, the inordinate delay of nearly 4 months in lodging the FIR has not been satisfactorily explained.

8. Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that the trial court has convicted the appellants without considering that the prosecutrix (PW-10) deposed that she went with the accused- appellants of her own volition and that she had contracted 'Nata' marriage with 'Bheria Meena' of her free will and lived with him for four months.
He argued that if she had lived with him for 4 months without complaining to anyone, the theory of abduction becomes out of question.

9. Learned counsel contended that the prosecutrix was not abducted or compelled to marry Bheria Meena, as in her oral testimony, she had clearly deposed that she was gleefully living with Bheria Meena and also that 'Nata' Marriage was a prevalent norm in her community and in that tribal area.

10. He further argued that the facts of the case clearly reveal that the prosecutrix had travelled along with the accused appellants through public transport and had stayed with Bheria for about four months and still she neither resisted nor informed the Police or even her neighbors that she had been forcefully confined.

11. It was argued that allegation of sexual assault committed upon her is also false and an afterthought inasmuch as in her statement given to the Police, she did not make a whisper about the rape being committed to the Police.

12. Learned counsel invited Court's attention towards the cross- examination of the prosecutrix and argued that when the prosecutrix was traced out, her father was present and if any (Uploaded on 06/10/2025 at 05:21:15 PM) (5 of 8) [CRLA-207/1996] sexual assault or crime had been committed,
she would at least inform her father about the same and the written report could have been lodged without any delay, whereas it took 8 days for the complainant to file the First Information Report.
13.

Learned counsel further argued that PW-2 - Babulal (brother in law) has clearly stated before the trial court that the whole ordeal was dictated to him by 'K' - the prosecutrix, but said statement also does not contain factum of commission of sexual assault on her.

14. Learned counsel relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court rendered in the case of Rajak Mohammad Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh reported in (2018) 9 SCC 248 in order to canvass that the prosecutrix had travelled with the appellants for a number of days and lived with Bheria for four months clearly showing that she was a consenting party.

sentences.text: He argued that the trial court has failed to appreciate the facts and evidence on record in its true perspective and has convicted the appellants for the offence which they never committed.

16. Having argued so, learned counsel Mr. Vyas concluded by saying that an absolutely false case has been lodged by the complainant maybe, because of being dissatisfied with the amount he might receive for the 'Nata', while reminding the court that it is a common phenomenon in that part of the State, where tribal women freely go with other persons under a 'Nata'.
17.

Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellants by contending that the trial Court has rightly convicted the accused (Uploaded on 06/10/2025 at 05:21:15 PM) (6 of 8) [CRLA-207/1996] and has made no error in appreciating the prosecution evidence.
He underscored that prosecutrix has unequivocally deposed and asserted that appellants had committed rape on her.

18. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and carefully examined the record, this Court is of the view that no case of conviction under Section 366 read with Section 120 B of the IPC is made out against the appellants.

Learned trial court has seriously erred in appreciating of the deposition made by the prosecutrix (PW-10), more particularly the part where she has stated that she was living contentedly with Bheria Meena, with whom she contracted a Nata Marriage, showing that she was under no compulsion.
19. She had multiple occasions to raise an alarm, but did not do the same, even when passing through multiple public places and travelling in public transport.
Her proven silence for 4 months is enough to demolish the case of abduction.

20. Furthermore, the conviction of the accused-appellants under section 120-B of the IPC is untenable as there was no prior agreement among the accused and they happened to meet the prosecutrix en-route.
So far as appellant no.1 - Kesu Ram is concerned, he joined the other co-accused persons at much later point of time, hence, in his case, it can not even be alleged.

21. The present case substantially rather solely rests on the testimony of the prosecutrix that she was forced to accompany the accused persons namely, Gautam, Sohan, Jagdish, Gopal by their wives en-route to her in-laws' place whereafter, she was made to get off the bus amidst the forest of Nimbaheda by the accused persons, who also alighted and committed rape on her.
(Uploaded on 06/10/2025 at 05:21:15 PM) (7 of 8)

22. The oral testimony of the prosecutrix which is the sole edifice for convicting the appellants does not inspire confidence inasmuch as she did not allege any sexual assault at the first instance, when she met her father and Babulal (PW-2), who came to take her from Dhakarkhedi.
She did not even allege sexual assault when she firstly met the Police and it was only thereafter, she changed her version and indicted the appellants of sexual assault.

sentences.text: The delay of four months in lodging the missing person report can still be understood, but the delay of 8 days in reporting the sexual assault that too by four persons remains unexplained by the prosecution.

24. In view of the aforesaid and considering that the prosecutrix was neither subjected to the medical examination nor could be subjected to, as the gang rape was allegedly committed by 4 persons 4 months ago, this Court is of the view that the accusation of sexual assault upon the appellants is not tenable.
Furthermore, there is no evidence on record sufficient to prove offence under Section 376 of the IPC, except the oral version of the prosecutrix, which too seems to be motivated.

25. That apart, the trial court has failed to appreciate the testimony of the prosecutrix in its entirety,
more particularly, in the backdrop of the social background of the appellants and the prosecutrix and the area where 'Nata - Pratha' is prevalent and a norm.

26. The trial court has also failed to take into account the prosecutrix's version in her cross-examination, where she has accepted that she did not apprise the Police about the sexual assault and that she had gleefully lived with Bheria, as his wife for (Uploaded on 06/10/2025 at 05:21:15 PM) (8 of 8) [CRLA-207/1996] four months and further that presently, she was living in Sanoti Village with another person - one Huma under 'Nata' and that too for past 5-6 years.

The fact that the prosecutrix has accepted that she has two husbands under a 'Nata', clearly shows that she has practically accepted the factum of going with Bheria under 'Nata' and therefore, the prosecution's case under Section 366 of the IPC falls flat on the ground.
27.
In view of the above discussion, this Court is satisfied that prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the appellants beyond reasonable doubt, rendering the conviction unsustainable.
28. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed.
29. The judgment and order dated 28.02.1996 impugned in the present appeal is quashed and set aside and the appellants are acquitted of all the charges.
Since, the appellants are on bail, the bail bonds of the appellants are hereby discharged.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 1-Arvind/-
